counts_when: The marks require expanding brackets, factorising, or simplifying a polynomial expression as a required step, not just collecting like terms (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Factorising only to solve a quadratic equation belongs to Quadratic equations; simplifying fractions with algebraic denominators belongs to Algebraic fractions.

counts_when: The marks require adding, subtracting, multiplying or simplifying fractions whose numerators or denominators contain algebra (common denominators, cancelling factors) (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Fractions that only contain numbers are arithmetic and get no tag; rationalising a surd denominator belongs to Surds and rationalising denominators.

counts_when: The marks require applying index laws to simplify or solve, including negative, zero and fractional indices (e.g. rewriting 1/(x√x) as x^(-3/2) is a step that counts only on Year 11 parts) (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Solving for an unknown index with logarithms belongs to Exponential equations.

counts_when: The marks require simplifying, expanding or rationalising expressions containing surds (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Leaving an answer in exact surd form without manipulating it gets no tag.

counts_when: Solving a linear equation or a linear inequality is the stated task of the part, or a linear inequality (sign flip, number line) must be solved as a step (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill); including solving a plain linear equation when that is the question
not_when: A one-line linear rearrangement inside a larger problem gets no tag; inequalities with x² belong to Quadratic inequalities.

counts_when: The marks require solving a quadratic equation (by factorising, completing the square or the formula), including equations that become quadratic after substitution in a Year 11 topic (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Quadratics in sin x or cos x belong to Quadratic trigonometric equations; deciding how many roots exist without solving belongs to Discriminant and the nature of roots.

counts_when: The marks require solving an inequality involving a quadratic expression (e.g. x² − 4 > 0 for a domain, or an interval of values of k) (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: A condition on the discriminant (Δ > 0, Δ < 0) also gets Discriminant and the nature of roots; reading the solution off a drawn graph belongs to Graphical solution of equations and inequalities.

skill: Discriminant and the nature of roots
aliases: The discriminant and the nature of roots
Use the discriminant to count roots
counts_when: The marks require using Δ = b² − 4ac to decide the number of real roots or x-intercepts, or to find the values of a parameter for which a quadratic has two, one or no real roots (including line–curve tangency and positive/negative definite conditions).
not_when: Solving the quadratic to find the actual roots belongs to Quadratic equations only.

counts_when: The marks require matching coefficients of two expressions that are equal for all x to find unknown constants.
not_when: Finding unknowns by substituting points into an equation belongs to Simultaneous equations.

counts_when: The marks require solving two (or more) equations simultaneously, algebraically, including finding intersection points of a line and a curve (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Reading intersection points off a given graph belongs to Graphical solution of equations and inequalities; a cost-revenue break-even problem also gets Linear models and break-even analysis.

aliases: Find the equation of a line
counts_when: The marks require finding or using the equation of a straight line (gradient, intercepts, gradient–intercept, general or point–gradient form) or graphing a line from its equation.
not_when: The equation of a tangent or normal to a curve belongs to Tangents and normals; a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line also gets Parallel and perpendicular lines.

counts_when: The marks require using equal gradients (parallel) or m₁m₂ = −1 (perpendicular) between two lines.
not_when: The gradient of a normal to a curve is part of Tangents and normals, not this skill.

skill: Angle of inclination of a line
aliases: Angle a line makes with the x-axis
counts_when: The marks require the relationship m = tan θ between a line's (or tangent's) gradient and the angle it makes with the positive x-axis.
not_when: Angles inside a triangle found with trig ratios belong to Right-angled trigonometry.

counts_when: The marks require building or using a linear function or linear inequality for a real-world situation (cost, revenue, profit, break-even, rates).
not_when: A model that is quadratic belongs to Quadratic models; a sequence that grows by a constant amount each term belongs to Terms of an arithmetic sequence.

counts_when: The marks require building or using a quadratic function in a real-world context (projectile height, area, profit) without calculus, e.g. maximum via the vertex.
not_when: Maximising a contextual function by differentiation belongs to Solving optimisation problems.

counts_when: The marks require forming y = kxⁿ or y = k/xⁿ from a 'varies directly/inversely' statement, finding k, or using the model.
not_when: A given linear formula used in context belongs to Linear models and break-even analysis.

aliases: Relations, functions and the vertical line test
Is it a function? (vertical line test)
counts_when: The marks require deciding whether a relation is a function (vertical line test, one-to-one / many-to-one) or identifying independent and dependent variables.
not_when: Finding the set of allowed x-values belongs to Domain and range.

counts_when: Evaluating or substituting into f( ) notation is the task of the part (f(3), f(a + h), f(x) = k given), not merely that the question names the function f (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Substituting into the formula of a named model (temperature, displacement) belongs to that model's skill.

counts_when: The marks require determining or stating the domain or range of a function or relation (natural domain from square roots, logs or denominators; range from the graph).
not_when: Range of a sin/cos function found from amplitude and centre line belongs to Amplitude, period and phase; writing the answer in interval form also gets Interval notation only on Year 11 parts.

counts_when: The question explicitly asks for, or gives, a set of values in interval notation [a, b), (−∞, c] that must be written or interpreted (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Stating the domain or range as an inequality belongs to Domain and range only.

counts_when: The marks require forming or evaluating f(g(x)), or finding the domain or range of a composite.
not_when: Differentiating a composite belongs to Chain rule.

counts_when: The marks require testing or using f(−x) = f(x) or f(−x) = −f(x), or the y-axis/origin symmetry of a graph, outside an integral.
not_when: Using symmetry to evaluate a definite integral belongs to Integrals of odd and even functions.

aliases: Where a graph is continuous or breaks
counts_when: The marks require identifying where a function is or is not continuous, or choosing a constant to make a function continuous.
not_when: A point where the curve is continuous but has a corner or cusp belongs to Differentiability.

counts_when: The marks require sketching or reading a parabola's features (vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts, concavity) or finding its equation from such features.
not_when: Solving a quadratic inequality without a graph belongs to Quadratic inequalities; a parabola after a stated transformation also gets Sketching transformed graphs.

skill: Graphs of cubic and polynomial functions
counts_when: The marks require sketching or identifying the graph of a polynomial from its factored form (intercepts, multiplicity, end behaviour), without derivatives.
not_when: Sketching a polynomial using stationary points and inflections belongs to Curve sketching using calculus.

counts_when: The marks require the graph or behaviour of the basic hyperbola y = k/x (shape, asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0, behaviour as x → ±∞).
not_when: A shifted hyperbola y = a/(x − h) + k belongs to Transformations of hyperbolas; other rational functions belong to Asymptotes and limiting behaviour.

counts_when: The marks require graphing or reading y = |x| or y = |ax + b| (vertex, symmetry, domain, range).
not_when: For |f(x)| with non-linear f, tag the skills actually used (e.g. Graphical solution of equations and inequalities, Transformations of trigonometric graphs) instead of this skill.

aliases: Solve absolute value equations and inequalities
counts_when: The marks require solving |ax + b| = k (or a simple linear absolute value inequality) algebraically or by checking solutions.
not_when: Solving |f(x)| = k for non-linear f from a graph belongs to Graphical solution of equations and inequalities.

counts_when: The marks require the equation or graph of a circle or semicircle, including completing the square to find centre and radius.
not_when: Arc, sector or segment measurements belong to Arc length, Area of a sector or Area of a segment.

counts_when: The marks require evaluating, graphing or interpreting a function defined by different rules on different parts of its domain.
not_when: Deciding only whether the pieces join belongs to Continuity and discontinuities; a pdf given piecewise belongs to the random-variable skills.

skill: Graphical solution of equations and inequalities
aliases: Solve equations and inequalities using graphs
counts_when: The marks require solving f(x) = k, f(x) = g(x) or an inequality by using graphs: reading intersections, counting solutions, or reading the x-values where one graph lies above another.
not_when: Solving a line and curve simultaneously by algebra belongs to Simultaneous equations; counting roots with Δ belongs to Discriminant and the nature of roots.

counts_when: The marks require applying or recognising a horizontal or vertical shift (x → x − a, y → y − b) of a non-trigonometric graph.
not_when: Phase or vertical shifts of sin, cos and tan belong to Amplitude, period and phase.

counts_when: The marks require applying or recognising a horizontal or vertical stretch or compression (x → x/k, y → y/k) of a non-trigonometric graph.
not_when: Changing the period or amplitude of a trig graph belongs to Amplitude, period and phase.

counts_when: The marks require applying or recognising a reflection in the x-axis (y = −f(x)) or y-axis (y = f(−x)) of a non-trigonometric graph.
not_when: Reflecting y = aˣ in y = x to get y = logₐx belongs to Graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions.

aliases: Combine transformations in the right order
counts_when: The marks require applying two or more transformations in sequence where the order matters, or identifying such a sequence.
not_when: A single transformation gets only its own type (Translations, Dilations or Reflections of graphs).

aliases: Write the equation of a transformed graph
counts_when: The marks require writing or choosing the equation of a graph after stated transformations, or finding the parameters of y = kf(a(x + b)) + c from a description or graph.
not_when: Producing a drawing belongs to Sketching transformed graphs; locating a single point's image belongs to Images of points under transformations.

aliases: Where a point moves under a transformation
counts_when: The marks require finding where a specific point (intercept, vertex, turning point) moves under a stated transformation.
not_when: Writing the whole transformed equation belongs to Equations of transformed functions.

counts_when: The marks require drawing the graph of a function obtained by transforming a given graph or equation (non-trigonometric).
not_when: Sketching transformed sin, cos or tan belongs to Transformations of trigonometric graphs.

counts_when: The marks require working with y = a/(x − h) + k (or a graph of it): its asymptotes, intercepts, equation or sketch; tag alongside the transformation type and task skills used.
not_when: Asymptotes of rational functions not of this form belong to Asymptotes and limiting behaviour; the untransformed y = k/x belongs to Hyperbolas and their asymptotes.

skill: Transformations of exponential and logarithmic graphs
counts_when: The marks require working with a transformed exponential or log graph (e.g. y = 2ˣ⁺¹ − 3, y = ln 3x): its asymptote, intercepts, equation or sketch; tag alongside the transformation type and task skills used.
not_when: The untransformed y = aˣ or y = logₐx belongs to Graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions.

counts_when: The marks require sin, cos or tan ratios (or Pythagoras with them) in a right-angled triangle to find a side or angle (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill); including Pythagoras on its own in a right-angled triangle
not_when: Non-right-angled triangles belong to Sine rule or Cosine rule; three-dimensional problems are removed (Year 11 Extension 1) and get no skill.

counts_when: The marks require exact values of trig ratios of 30°, 45°, 60° (π/6, π/4, π/3) or multiples of 90° (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Exact values at related angles in other quadrants also get Related and complementary angles only on Year 11 parts.

counts_when: The marks require interpreting an angle of elevation or depression in a two-dimensional diagram; tag with the triangle rule used.
not_when: Elevation problems in three dimensions (towers seen from two points, pyramids) are removed, not tagged.

counts_when: The marks require interpreting or finding a true or compass bearing in a two-dimensional navigation problem; tag with the triangle rule(s) used.
not_when: An angle inside a triangle with no bearing to read or state belongs only to the triangle rule used.

counts_when: The marks require a/sin A = b/sin B to find a side or angle in a non-right-angled triangle (when either rule would find an angle, tag the rule already used earlier in the same part, otherwise Sine rule).
not_when: Two possible obtuse/acute answers belong to Ambiguous case of the sine rule; two sides and the included angle need Cosine rule.

skill: Ambiguous case of the sine rule
aliases: The ambiguous case of the sine rule
counts_when: The marks require recognising or finding both possible angles (acute and obtuse) when the sine rule is used to find an angle.
not_when: A sine-rule angle where the obtuse case is impossible or not asked belongs to Sine rule only.

counts_when: The marks require c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C (or its angle form) in a non-right-angled triangle.
not_when: A right-angled triangle uses Pythagoras/Right-angled trigonometry, not this skill.

skill: Area of a triangle (½ab sin C)
aliases: Area of a triangle ½ab sin C
counts_when: The marks require the formula A = ½ab sin C for a triangle's area.
not_when: Area of a segment (sector minus triangle) belongs to Area of a segment only.

counts_when: The marks require converting between degrees and radians or using the definition of a radian (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Using θ in radians inside l = rθ or A = ½r²θ belongs to Arc length or Area of a sector.

counts_when: The marks require l = rθ (θ in radians), including perimeters of sectors.
not_when: Areas of sectors belong to Area of a sector.

counts_when: The marks require A = ½r²θ for a sector (major or minor) on its own.
not_when: Sector minus triangle (segment) belongs to Area of a segment, which is tagged instead.

counts_when: The marks require the area of a circular segment, ½r²(θ − sin θ) or sector minus triangle; do not also tag Area of a sector or Area of a triangle (½ab sin C).
not_when: A whole sector with no triangle removed belongs to Area of a sector.

aliases: Graphs of sin, cos and tan
counts_when: The marks require sketching or reading the basic graphs y = sin x, cos x, tan x (intercepts, asymptotes, period 2π or π) with no transformation. Also sketching or reading y = sec x, cosec x or cot x (owner 12 Nov: no 2024 dot point; filed under the trig-graph dot point with a note).
not_when: Graphs with changed amplitude, period or shift belong to Transformations of trigonometric graphs.

counts_when: The marks require defining, evaluating or rewriting sec, cosec or cot in terms of sin, cos, tan (e.g. cot 2x = cos 2x / sin 2x before integrating).
not_when: Differentiating sec, cosec or cot directly from the standard results belongs to Derivatives of trigonometric functions.

counts_when: The marks require using sin²x + cos²x = 1, 1 + tan²x = sec²x or 1 + cot²x = cosec²x to rewrite an expression or equation.
not_when: Writing a full LHS = RHS proof also gets Proving trigonometric identities.

counts_when: The part asks to prove or show that one trigonometric expression is identically equal to another; tag with the identities used.
not_when: A 'show that' about a derivative or integral is not an identity proof and belongs to the calculus skill used.

counts_when: The marks require evaluating a trig ratio of an angle of any magnitude via its related angle (ASTC), or using sin(90° − θ) = cos θ or f(−θ) results, other than finding the quadrant solutions of a trig equation (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Finding all solutions of a trig equation in a domain belongs to Trigonometric equations, which covers the ASTC step.

counts_when: The marks require solving an equation (or inequality) in sin, cos or tan of a linear argument on a restricted domain, including sin(bx + c) = k with an adjusted domain. Dot point (owner 12 Nov): sin x, cos x or tan x of x alone (sin x = k) -> Y11-101; any transformed argument sin(bx + c) with b ≠ 1 or c ≠ 0 -> Y12-204, which makes the part Year 12.
not_when: An equation that is a quadratic in a trig ratio belongs to Quadratic trigonometric equations instead.

counts_when: The marks require solving an equation that reduces to a quadratic in sin x, cos x or tan x (including after a Pythagorean identity substitution, which also gets Pythagorean identities).
not_when: A single linear trig equation belongs to Trigonometric equations; do not tag both.

counts_when: The marks require the log laws (product, quotient, power, logₐa = 1, logₐ1 = 0) to simplify, evaluate or solve (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Using log laws to simplify before differentiating belongs to Logarithm laws in differentiation.

counts_when: The marks require logₐx = log_b x / log_b a to evaluate or rewrite a logarithm (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Differentiating logₐx belongs to Derivatives of logarithmic functions.

counts_when: The marks require solving an equation with the unknown in an index (aˣ = b, e^(kt) = c, or a quadratic in eˣ) using logs or equal bases (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Solving for the number of loan or annuity payments belongs to Number of payments using logarithms; finding k or t in Q = Ae^(kt) belongs to Exponential growth and decay.

counts_when: The marks require solving an equation containing logarithms of the unknown (e.g. log₂x + log₂(x − 2) = 3), including checking for invalid solutions (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: An equation with the unknown only in an index belongs to Exponential equations.

skill: Graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions
counts_when: The marks require sketching or reading the basic graphs y = aˣ, y = a⁻ˣ, y = logₐx (intercepts, asymptotes, behaviour as x → ±∞, reflection in y = x).
not_when: Shifted or stretched exponential/log graphs belong to Transformations of exponential and logarithmic graphs.

aliases: Euler's number and the natural logarithm
e and the natural log ln
counts_when: The marks require the definition or properties of e and ln (ln e = 1, e^(ln x) = x, d/dx eˣ = eˣ as a definition, evaluating e or ln values) (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: Differentiating eˣ in a Year 12 context belongs to Derivatives of exponential functions.

aliases: Gradient and average rate of change
counts_when: The marks require Δy/Δx over an interval: the gradient of a secant, an average speed, or an estimate of an instantaneous rate from a graph or table.
not_when: An exact instantaneous rate from a derivative belongs to Rates of change (or Velocity as a rate of change for motion).

counts_when: The part requires the limit definition f′(x) = lim (f(x + h) − f(x))/h to find or justify a derivative.
not_when: Using the power rule when first principles are not demanded belongs to Differentiation of powers of x.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating terms kxⁿ (any real n, after rewriting roots and reciprocals) and sums of them (Year 11 basic: never tagged on a part that needs any Year 12 skill).
not_when: A power of a bracket (ax + b)ⁿ that is not expanded also gets Chain rule.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating a composite function, including powers of brackets and any exp, log or trig function of a non-linear inner function (e^(x²), ln(2x² − 5), cos(ln x)).
not_when: Exp, log or trig of a linear inner function (e^(3x), sin(2x + 1), ln(5x)) is covered by the Year 12 derivative skills alone; an integral of f′(x)[f(x)]ⁿ belongs to Reverse chain rule.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating a product of two non-constant functions with d(uv)/dx = u′v + uv′.
not_when: A log of a product that is split with log laws first belongs to Logarithm laws in differentiation instead.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating a quotient u/v with the quotient rule (where v is not a constant or a simple power of x that can be rewritten).
not_when: A log of a quotient split with log laws belongs to Logarithm laws in differentiation; tan x from sin x / cos x is part of Derivatives of trigonometric functions unless the proof is asked.

aliases: Equation of a tangent or normal
counts_when: The marks require the equation of a tangent or normal to a curve, or finding points where the tangent/normal has a given gradient or passes through a given point (any function type; tag the derivative skill too).
not_when: A line not linked to a curve's derivative belongs to Equations of straight lines.

aliases: Where a function increases or decreases
counts_when: The marks require using the sign of f′(x) to find or justify where a function is increasing or decreasing.
not_when: Reading where f is increasing from a given graph of f′ belongs to Graphs of f, f′ and f″; classifying a stationary point belongs to Stationary points and their nature.

skill: Velocity as a rate of change
counts_when: The marks require velocity or speed as dx/dt of a displacement made of powers of t only, with no acceleration, integration or Year 12 functions.
not_when: Any motion part with acceleration, integration, or exp/log/trig displacement belongs to Displacement, velocity and acceleration.

skill: Sample spaces and equally likely outcomes
counts_when: The marks require listing or counting a sample space (list, grid, table of outcomes) and using P = favourable/total for equally likely outcomes.
not_when: Counting by multiplying the number of choices for each position belongs to Multiplication principle.

counts_when: The marks require counting outcomes by multiplying the number of choices at each stage (codes, PINs, arrangements).
not_when: Multiplying probabilities along branches belongs to Multistage events and tree diagrams.

counts_when: The marks require drawing or reading a Venn diagram, or using set notation and |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B| for counts.
not_when: Probability formula P(A ∪ B) used without a diagram belongs to Addition rule and mutually exclusive events.

counts_when: The marks require completing or reading a two-way (contingency) table of counts or probabilities.
not_when: A table listing the outcomes of two dice/spinners belongs to Sample spaces and equally likely outcomes.

skill: Addition rule and mutually exclusive events
aliases: The addition rule and mutually exclusive events
counts_when: The marks require P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B) or adding probabilities of mutually exclusive events as the method (beyond adding branch totals of a tree).
not_when: Adding the end-branch probabilities of a tree is part of Multistage events and tree diagrams.

counts_when: The marks require P(not A) = 1 − P(A) other than for an 'at least one' event.
not_when: 1 − P(none) for 'at least one' belongs to 'At least one' probabilities instead.

counts_when: The marks require P(A | B) by any method (formula, restricted sample space, table, tree or a probability distribution).
not_when: A second-stage branch probability that is simply given (e.g. without replacement) belongs to Multistage events and tree diagrams.

counts_when: The marks require testing or proving independence, or using P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) for two named events stated to be independent.
not_when: Multiplying probabilities of repeated independent trials (games, spins, draws with replacement) belongs to Multistage events and tree diagrams.

counts_when: The marks require combining probabilities over two or more stages or trials by multiplying along paths and adding paths (tree, array, with or without replacement).
not_when: Testing whether two events are independent belongs to Independent events.

counts_when: The marks require the probability of 'at least one' (usually 1 − P(none)); do not also tag Complementary events.
not_when: 'Exactly one' or other counts of successes belong to Multistage events and tree diagrams.

counts_when: The marks require the expected number of occurrences as n × p (in any context, including normal distributions).
not_when: The mean of a random variable ΣxP(x) belongs to Expected value.

counts_when: The marks require estimating a probability from experimental results or data as frequency ÷ total.
not_when: Theoretical probabilities from equally likely outcomes belong to Sample spaces and equally likely outcomes.

counts_when: The marks require building or reading a frequency, relative frequency or cumulative frequency table, histogram or polygon.
not_when: Quartiles, box plots, standard deviation of a data set and bivariate data are removed, not tagged; a probability distribution table belongs to Discrete probability distributions.

aliases: nth term of an arithmetic sequence
counts_when: The marks require Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d (find a term, a, d, or n, or whether a value is a term).
not_when: Showing three given terms are in AP or finding an unknown from 2b = a + c belongs to Testing for arithmetic and geometric sequences.

counts_when: The marks require Sₙ = n/2(a + l) or n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] (find a sum, or n given a sum).
not_when: Finding a single term belongs to Terms of an arithmetic sequence.

aliases: nth term of a geometric sequence
counts_when: The marks require Tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹ (find a term, a, r, or n).
not_when: Finding r from the equal-ratio condition b/a = c/b belongs to Testing for arithmetic and geometric sequences.

counts_when: The marks require Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) or summing a finite GP, including the GP sum inside an annuity or loan formula.
not_when: An infinite sum belongs to Limiting sums.

skill: Testing for arithmetic and geometric sequences
aliases: Show terms are arithmetic or geometric
counts_when: The marks require showing a sequence or series is arithmetic or geometric (constant difference or ratio), or using 2b = a + c or b² = ac to find an unknown or the common ratio.
not_when: Finding a later term once a and d (or r) are known belongs to Terms of an arithmetic sequence or Terms of a geometric sequence.

counts_when: The marks require S∞ = a/(1 − r) or the condition |r| < 1 for a limiting sum to exist.
not_when: Converting a recurring decimal to a fraction also gets Recurring decimals as limiting sums.

counts_when: The marks require writing a recurring decimal as a geometric series and evaluating its limiting sum.
not_when: Other limiting sums belong to Limiting sums only.

counts_when: The marks require reading, writing or evaluating a sum written in Σ notation (number of terms, first term, value).
not_when: A sum written out term by term belongs to Arithmetic series or Geometric series only.

skill: Applications of arithmetic and geometric sequences
counts_when: The marks require identifying an AP or GP from a worded context (seats in rows, distance run, bouncing ball, stacked objects) and are tagged with the term or sum skill used. Includes a bouncing ball or any object rebounding to a fixed fraction or percentage of its previous height (owner 12 Nov).
not_when: Repeated percentage growth/decay belongs to Geometric growth and decay; money with interest belongs to the Financial mathematics skills.

aliases: Growth and decay as a sequence
counts_when: The marks require modelling a quantity that changes by a constant percentage or factor each period as a GP term arⁿ⁻¹ (populations, depreciation, production), outside finance.
not_when: Money invested at compound interest belongs to Compound interest; continuous growth Q = Ae^(kt) belongs to Exponential growth and decay. A bouncing or rebounding object belongs to Applications of arithmetic and geometric sequences (owner 12 Nov).

counts_when: The marks require A = P(1 + r)ⁿ for a single sum (find A, P, r, n or the interest), with the rate and compounding period converted.
not_when: Regular repeated payments belong to the Annuities or Reducing balance loans skills; interest-factor table look-ups are removed.

counts_when: The marks require discounting a future amount to its present value (dividing by (1 + r)ⁿ) or comparing or summing amounts at different times, including the present value of a stream of withdrawals.
not_when: Growing a single principal forward only belongs to Compound interest.

counts_when: The marks concern an investment built by regular equal deposits with compound interest (future value, deposit size, balance after n periods); tag with the method skill used (Geometric series or Recurrence relations).
not_when: A single lump sum with no further deposits belongs to Compound interest.

counts_when: The marks concern a fund drawn down by regular equal withdrawals (amount needed, withdrawal size, time the fund lasts); tag with the method skill used.
not_when: Repaying a borrowed amount belongs to Reducing balance loans.

counts_when: The marks concern a loan repaid by regular equal repayments with interest on the balance (amount owing, repayment size, total paid); tag with the method skill used.
not_when: A savings fund that pays out regular amounts belongs to Annuities: withdrawals.

aliases: Recurrence relations for loans and annuities
counts_when: The marks require writing, using or iterating a recurrence relation (next term from the previous one): loan or annuity balances A_{n+1} = A_n(1 + r) ± M, and also non-finance models such as populations, medication doses or repeated percentage change with additions (owner 12 Nov: widened beyond finance).
not_when: Summing the resulting GP to get a closed form belongs to Geometric series (tag both if the part does both).

counts_when: The marks require solving for the number of payments or periods n in a loan or annuity (or compound interest) equation using logarithms.
not_when: Solving an exponential equation outside finance belongs to Exponential equations or Exponential growth and decay.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating eˣ, e^(ax+b), e^(f(x)) or aˣ.
not_when: Integrating these belongs to Integrals of exponential functions.

aliases: Differentiate logs ln x and logₐx
counts_when: The marks require differentiating ln x, ln(f(x)) or logₐx.
not_when: Integrals that give a logarithm belong to Integrals giving logarithms.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating sin, cos, tan (or sec, cosec, cot) of x or of an inner function.
not_when: Rewriting sec, cosec or cot in terms of sin/cos to simplify also gets Reciprocal trigonometric ratios.

counts_when: The function differentiated is a log of a product, quotient, power or root (ln((x + 1)/(x − 2)), ln√(2x² − 5)), so the marks require expanding it with log laws first; do not also tag Product rule or Quotient rule for it.
not_when: Log laws used to solve an equation belong to Logarithm laws.

counts_when: The marks require a derivative as an instantaneous rate in a non-motion practical context (dV/dt, dP/dt, d²Q/dt² and the meaning of their signs).
not_when: Particle motion belongs to Displacement, velocity and acceleration; dQ/dt = kQ belongs to Exponential growth and decay; integrating a given rate belongs to Rates of change using integration.

counts_when: The marks require computing f″(x) or d²y/dx² (on its own, or as a step in a concavity, second derivative test or acceleration).
not_when: Interpreting the sign of f″ for concavity also gets Concavity and points of inflection.

aliases: When a function can be differentiated
counts_when: The marks require deciding where a function is continuous but not differentiable (corners, cusps, vertical tangents) or using the limit definition at a point.
not_when: Points where the function is not continuous belong to Continuity and discontinuities.

aliases: Find stationary points: max, min or inflection
counts_when: The marks require finding where f′(x) = 0 and/or classifying a stationary point as maximum, minimum or horizontal inflection by any method (including from a graph of f′).
not_when: When the classification must use f″ also tag Second derivative test; in a worded optimisation problem tag Solving optimisation problems instead.

counts_when: The classification of a stationary point must use the sign of f″ at that point (the question says so, or f″ was found for this purpose).
not_when: Classifying by a table of f′ values belongs to Stationary points and their nature only; a free choice of method gets Stationary points and their nature only.

counts_when: The marks require intervals of concavity from the sign of f″, or finding and justifying points of inflection (f″ = 0 with a change of concavity).
not_when: A horizontal point of inflection found by a table of f′ values belongs to Stationary points and their nature.

counts_when: The part asks for a sketch whose features come from derivatives (stationary points, inflections, asymptotes), including general rational functions; also tag the feature skills found within the same part.
not_when: Sketching a polynomial from its factors alone belongs to Graphs of cubic and polynomial functions; features found in earlier parts are not re-tagged on a 'hence sketch' part.

aliases: Asymptotes and behaviour as x gets large
counts_when: The marks require vertical or horizontal asymptotes of a function other than a (transformed) hyperbola y = a/(x − h) + k, or a limit as x or t → ±∞ (including limiting velocity or population).
not_when: Asymptotes of y = k/x belong to Hyperbolas and their asymptotes; of y = a/(x − h) + k to Transformations of hyperbolas.

aliases: Greatest and least value on an interval
counts_when: The marks require the greatest or least value of a function on a closed or restricted domain, comparing stationary values with endpoint values.
not_when: A local maximum with no endpoint check belongs to Stationary points and their nature.

skill: Maxima and minima from the range
aliases: Maxima and minima from the range of a function
Max or min using the range of a function
counts_when: The marks require finding a maximum or minimum without calculus from the known range of a function (e.g. −1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1, a squared term ≥ 0).
not_when: A maximum found by differentiating belongs to Stationary points and their nature or Solving optimisation problems.

counts_when: The marks require building the expression to be optimised from a description or diagram (defining variables, using a constraint to reduce to one variable, 'show that A = …').
not_when: Differentiating a given expression to find the optimum belongs to Solving optimisation problems.

counts_when: The marks require differentiating a contextual function to find and justify the optimum value or the variable that gives it; do not also tag Stationary points and their nature or Second derivative test.
not_when: Building the function belongs to Setting up optimisation problems; a maximum from the vertex of a quadratic model without calculus belongs to Quadratic models.

counts_when: The marks require moving between x, v and a for a particle in a straight line by differentiation or integration, or interpreting position, velocity, speed or acceleration values (any part beyond Velocity as a rate of change).
not_when: Times when v = 0 or the direction changes belong to Particles at rest and changing direction; information read from an x–t or v–t graph belongs to Motion graphs.

skill: Particles at rest and changing direction
aliases: When a particle is at rest or turns
counts_when: The marks require finding when or where a particle is at rest (v = 0) or changes direction (v changes sign).
not_when: Total distance using those turning times also gets Distance travelled.

counts_when: The marks require the total distance travelled over a time interval, accounting for changes of direction (from positions, integration of |v|, or areas under a v–t graph).
not_when: Net change in position (displacement) belongs to Displacement, velocity and acceleration.

counts_when: The marks require drawing or reading a displacement–time or velocity–time graph (signs of v and a, gradients, areas, when at rest); including acceleration–time graphs
not_when: Motion given only by formulas belongs to Displacement, velocity and acceleration.

counts_when: The marks require the model dQ/dt = kQ or Q = Ae^(kt) (verify it, find A or k, half-life, a value, a time, or the rate dQ/dt).
not_when: Models with an added constant (Newton's cooling T = T₀ + Ae^(−kt)), logistic or log-scale models belong to Exponential and logarithmic models; discrete percentage growth belongs to Geometric growth and decay.

aliases: Rate of change problems using integration
counts_when: The marks require integrating a given non-motion rate dQ/dt to find a quantity or its change (flow, production, demand).
not_when: Integrating acceleration or velocity belongs to Displacement, velocity and acceleration; determining the constant also gets Primitives with initial conditions.

skill: Graphs of f, f′ and f″
aliases: Link the graphs of f, f′ and f″
counts_when: The marks require sketching or reasoning from the graph of one of f, f′, f″ to another (e.g. sketch f′ from f, deduce turning points or concavity of f from a graph of f′); in either direction, including sketching or describing f from a given graph of f′
not_when: Finding derivatives from a formula belongs to the differentiation and Stationary points skills.

counts_when: The marks require a primitive of terms kxⁿ (n ≠ −1, after rewriting roots and fractions), in an indefinite or definite integral, including recognising that primitives differ by a constant.
not_when: A power of a linear or inner function, (ax + b)ⁿ or f′(x)[f(x)]ⁿ, belongs to Reverse chain rule; 1/x belongs to Integrals giving logarithms.

aliases: Integrate using the reverse chain rule
counts_when: The marks require integrating (ax + b)ⁿ or f′(x)[f(x)]ⁿ (n ≠ −1).
not_when: f′(x)e^(f(x)), f′(x)/f(x) and f′(x)sin f(x) forms belong to the exponential, log and trig integral skills only.

counts_when: The marks require a primitive of eˣ, e^(ax+b), aˣ or f′(x)e^(f(x)).
not_when: Differentiating exponentials belongs to Derivatives of exponential functions.

counts_when: The marks require a primitive of 1/x, 1/(ax + b) or f′(x)/f(x) (including tan x or cot x written as a quotient).
not_when: A quotient whose numerator is not a multiple of the denominator's derivative and that splits into powers belongs to Indefinite integrals.

counts_when: The marks require a primitive of sin, cos or sec² of x, of ax + b, or of f(x) with its derivative present.
not_when: Rewriting cot or tan as a quotient to get a log belongs to Integrals giving logarithms.

counts_when: The marks require evaluating ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx as F(b) − F(a), in any setting (areas, volumes, probabilities, motion); tag with the primitive skill used.
not_when: An integral evaluated only by geometry (triangle, semicircle areas) belongs to Area under a curve or Areas below the x-axis.

counts_when: The marks require reversing limits, splitting or joining intervals, or linearity using given integral values (∫ₐᵇ f = 3, find ∫ₐᵇ (2f + 1)).
not_when: Using odd/even symmetry belongs to Integrals of odd and even functions.

skill: Integrals of odd and even functions
aliases: Odd and even functions in integrals
counts_when: The marks require using odd or even symmetry to evaluate or simplify a definite integral over [−a, a].
not_when: Testing a function for oddness/evenness with no integral belongs to Odd and even functions.

counts_when: The marks require the area between a curve and the x-axis where the curve stays on or above the axis over the interval (by integration or geometry).
not_when: A region partly or wholly below the x-axis belongs to Areas below the x-axis; between two curves belongs to Area between curves.

aliases: Area when the curve goes below the x-axis
counts_when: The marks require handling a region below the x-axis or a signed integral across a sign change (splitting at the root, absolute values, or net vs total area).
not_when: A region entirely above the axis belongs to Area under a curve only.

counts_when: The marks require the area of a region bounded by two curves (or a curve and a line), as ∫(upper − lower).
not_when: A region bounded by one curve and the x-axis belongs to Area under a curve or Areas below the x-axis.

skill: Area with respect to the y-axis
counts_when: The marks require integrating with respect to y (x = g(y)) or using the inverse/reflection of y = aˣ and y = logₐx to find an area.
not_when: Areas bounded by the x-axis integrated in x belong to Area under a curve.

counts_when: The marks require approximating an integral or area with the trapezoidal rule, or judging whether it over- or under-estimates.
not_when: An exact evaluation belongs to Definite integrals; do not tag the function-type integral skills for the approximation.

counts_when: A previous result d/dx[g(x)] = h(x) must be reversed to integrate h or a related function ('hence find ∫…'), including integration of ln x via a given derivative. For "hence or otherwise": if a standard primitive method also works, that method is required and this skill is can-use; if the given derivative is the only realistic route (e.g. ∫cosec x(1 − x cot x)dx after d/dx(x cosec x)), this skill is required (owner 12 Nov).
not_when: Integrals with a standard primitive formula belong to the relevant integral skill only.

aliases: Find the constant using a known point
counts_when: The marks require finding the constant of integration from a given value (f(a) = b, initial velocity, initial amount), in any context.
not_when: A definite integral (no constant to find) belongs to Definite integrals.

counts_when: The marks require a volume (or capacity) as cross-sectional area × length for a prism-like solid, usually with the area found by integration.
not_when: The cross-sectional area alone belongs to the area skills; volumes of revolution are not Advanced.

aliases: Amplitude, period, phase shift, centre line
counts_when: The marks require identifying or finding a, b, c, d in y = a sin(b(x + c)) + d (or cos, tan): amplitude, period, phase shift, centre line, or the resulting range/max/min.
not_when: Drawing the transformed graph also gets Transformations of trigonometric graphs; non-trig shifts belong to Translations of graphs.

counts_when: The marks require sketching a transformed sin, cos or tan graph, or matching a transformed trig graph to its equation, including graphical problems such as counting solutions of a trig equation from its graph.
not_when: Only stating amplitude, period or phase belongs to Amplitude, period and phase; untransformed trig graphs belong to Graphs of trigonometric functions.

aliases: Trig models: tides, daylight, Ferris wheels
counts_when: The marks concern a periodic real-world situation (tides, daylight, Ferris wheel, temperature) modelled by a trig function; tag with Amplitude, period and phase or Trigonometric equations as used.
not_when: A trig function with no real-world context gets only the trig skills used.

aliases: Exponential and log models: cooling, decibels
counts_when: The marks concern a given exponential or log model that is not plain Q = Ae^(kt): Newton's cooling, logistic-type, decibels, Richter or pH scales, or evaluating/interpreting such a model; including y = ka^t models in continuous time (a battery, a population over time) that are not written as a GP
not_when: Q = Ae^(kt) or dQ/dt = kQ belongs to Exponential growth and decay.

counts_when: The marks require completing, constructing or reading a discrete probability distribution (ΣP = 1, P(X = x), P(X in a range)), or classifying a variable as discrete/continuous. Includes the mode of a discrete distribution (the value with the highest probability) (owner 12 Nov).
not_when: Computing ΣxP(x) belongs to Expected value; an empirical frequency table of data belongs to Frequency tables and histograms.

counts_when: The marks require E(X) for a discrete (ΣxP(x)) or continuous (∫x f(x)dx) random variable, or using a given mean to find unknowns.
not_when: The expected number of successes n × p belongs to Expected frequency.

aliases: Variance and standard deviation of a random variable
Variance and standard deviation of X
counts_when: The marks require Var(X) or σ of a random variable (discrete or continuous), via E(X²) − μ² or Σ(x − μ)²P(x).
not_when: The standard deviation of a raw data set is removed content; a given σ used in a z-score belongs to z-scores.

counts_when: The marks require the properties of a pdf (f(x) ≥ 0, total area 1) to find a constant or verify a pdf, including the uniform pdf 1/(b − a); including probabilities or total area found by geometry (rectangles, triangles, trapezia) under a pdf
not_when: Computing a probability from a valid pdf belongs to Probabilities from a probability density function.

skill: Probabilities from a probability density function
counts_when: The marks require P(a < X < b) for a continuous variable by integrating a pdf or finding an area under it (and P(X = a) = 0).
not_when: Reading a probability straight from a cdf F(b) − F(a) belongs to Cumulative distribution functions.

counts_when: The marks require finding, graphing or using a cdf F(x) (F(x) = ∫f(t)dt, probabilities from F, or the pdf as F′(x)).
not_when: Finding the median from F(m) = 0.5 also gets Median, mode and percentiles of a pdf. Building F(x) = ∫ₐˣ f(t)dt from a pdf is this skill only, not also Integral as a function of its upper limit (owner 12 Nov).

skill: Median, mode and percentiles of a pdf
aliases: Mode, median and percentiles of continuous distributions
Mode, median and percentiles of a pdf
counts_when: The marks require the mode (maximum of the pdf), the median, quartiles or a percentile of a continuous random variable.
not_when: The mean of a continuous variable belongs to Expected value.

skill: Normal distribution and the empirical rule
aliases: The normal distribution and the empirical rule
counts_when: The marks require the 68–95–99.7% rule or the shape/symmetry of the normal curve (including its maximum and inflection points) to find or judge probabilities.
not_when: Probabilities from a z-table belong to Standard normal tables.

counts_when: The marks require computing z = (x − μ)/σ or converting a z-score back to a score, or interpreting it as a number of standard deviations (tag whenever a z-score is calculated).
not_when: Turning a z-score into a probability also gets Standard normal tables or Normal distribution and the empirical rule.

counts_when: The marks require reading probabilities from a standard normal (z) table, including symmetry to handle negative z or 'between' regions.
not_when: Probabilities from 68–95–99.7 belong to Normal distribution and the empirical rule.

counts_when: The marks require comparing results from different distributions via their z-scores and stating which is better or worse.
not_when: A single z-score calculation with no comparison belongs to z-scores only.

aliases: Find a value from a probability (inverse normal)
counts_when: The marks start from a probability or percentage and require finding a score, the mean or the standard deviation of a normal distribution.
not_when: Starting from a score and finding a probability belongs to Standard normal tables or Normal distribution and the empirical rule.

skill: Integral as a function of its upper limit
aliases: A(x) = integral from a to x
counts_when: The marks require treating A(x) = ∫ₐˣ f(t)dt as a function of x: differentiating it (A′(x) = f(x)), recognising it as a primitive, or reading its features from the graph of f.
not_when: Evaluating an integral with two numerical limits belongs to Definite integrals. Building a CDF from a pdf belongs to Cumulative distribution functions only.

aliases: find a term from the sum formula
counts_when: The marks require finding a term or the first term from a given partial-sum formula: T₁ = S₁, Tₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ (owner 12 Nov).
not_when: Summing terms with the AP or GP sum formula belongs to Arithmetic series or Geometric series.
